source_verification.title: A novel TRPC6 mutation that causes childhood FSGS
Identification and functional analysis of a novel TRPC6 mutation associated with late onset familial focal segmental glomerulosclerosis in Chinese patients

second_answer_attack.resolution: INF2 variants can cause familial FSGS through actin/cytoskeletal dysregulation, but the stem directly demonstrates a heterozygous TRPC6 variant with increased agonist-evoked current and delayed inactivation. That functional gain identifies excessive TRPC6 calcium entry as the proximal lesion.

blind_audit.rationale: TRPC6 is a calcium-permeable nonselective cation channel expressed in podocytes. Disease-causing dominant variants can increase channel activity or impair inactivation, producing excessive calcium influx and downstream signaling that disrupts podocyte structure and promotes FSGS. Strongest alternative resolved: INF2 variants can cause familial FSGS through actin/cytoskeletal dysregulation, but the stem directly demonstrates a heterozygous TRPC6 variant with increased agonist-evoked current and delayed inactivation. That functional gain identifies excessive TRPC6 calcium entry as the proximal lesion.
